newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir reserves judgement on Muhammad case.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir reserves judgement on Muhammad case.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he would not make any judgement on a government chief minister who was arrested in Australia for allegedly trying to take money out of the country without permission, Bernama news agency reported.

"I uphold the principle that a person is innocent until proven guilty," the Prime Minister told reporters in the northern island of Langkawi, when asked to comment on the case involving Selangor Chief Minister Muhammad Muhammad Taib.

Muhammad was stopped at Australia's Brisbane airport on December 22 as he was about to leave for New Zealand, allegedly carrying about A$1.2 million ($960,000) in Malaysian, Singaporean and New Zealand dollars.
Under Australian law, people leaving the country must declare and justify any amount worth over A$5,000 taken out, in whatever currency.
Mahathir said he was waiting for a report on the case from Muhammad, who has not contacted him directly.
Earlier this week, officials of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) said Mahathir has asked Muhammad to give him a report on the incident.
Muhammad is a vice-president of UMNO, of which Mahathir is its president.

Asked to comment on speculation that the money was linked with UMNO's internal elections in October, Mahathir said he would like to get the true picture first before making any statements, Bernama said.
UMNO held its biennial elections to choose party leaders last October with rumours that some leaders paid out money to party delegates to win election.
Muhammad was released unconditionally by Brisbane police after the arrest but has to reappear there for a hearing on March 31. Malaysian officials said on Friday he was currently in New Zealand.
